about: workflow:keep-a-short-list: keep a short list in the person's own store as one small head that names its items in order, and one record per item, so that adding an item writes that item and the head and never the whole list again; read the list in order, read only what is new after a position, and keep the counts of the fields the list names. It replaces the record-store half of tools/keep-a-short-list/src/kept-list.mjs, whose whole job was keeping these lists in the retired record store (rule a-tool-is-only-what-the-store-cannot-do).

payload.label: Keep a short list
payload.job: Keep a short list in the person's own store as a head that names its items in order plus one record per item, write only what changed, and read the list in order or only what is new after a position, from the store's own objects.
payload.produces: The store's own objects for a short list, proven on the example attempts, and each put of the list kept, repeated or refused and read back.

source.from: the owner, 2026-11-18 about 10:57 and 11:01 AM CST: a tool whose whole job is keeping records is a shortcut of what an AI does anyway
source.note: No tool keeps or reads the list: the run speaks to the person's store in its own language, and the store's own keys, checks and indexes hold the rules the intent below states. Each item is kept alone so that a change to one item never rewrites the others, and so that a reader that keeps the last position it saw reads nothing more when nothing was added. Every record a list keeps carries the list's own type, so a search or a mention that leaves the type out leaves the whole list out.

where.description: Where the person keeps these things: the store's own address

language.description: How that store is spoken to, in its own terms

credential_name.description: The vault name of the login the run uses, when it needs one

place.description: Where in the store the list is kept, when it already is

list.description: The list's name: lowercase letters, digits and dashes, up to 64 characters

items.description: The whole list as it should now be, in order, each item with its own seq (a whole number, unique in the list) and its fields

indexed_fields.description: Item fields whose value counts are kept on the head, so one can be asked for without reading the items

steps.title: Read what the store already keeps
steps.do: Speak to store in its own language, with the login under its credential_name, and read its own description of what it holds. Submit where short lists are already kept (kept_in, or null) and the names of the objects that already keep and show them.

steps.title: Make the store's own objects, once
steps.do: When the look step found nothing, make the store's own objects in its own form, so that the store itself refuses what the intent refuses wherever it can (keys, checks), with an index on each list's items by seq for reading what is new after a position. Grant only what the store's holder allows the person's login. Head, kept once per list: the item ids in order and, when indexed_fields are named, the count of each value of each named field. Item, kept once per list and seq: its item as the caller gives it, with the list's type on it. Keeping a put: an item whose seq is missing is refused, and so is a seq used twice in one put. An item that is new or differs from the one kept at its seq is written; an item kept at a seq the new put leaves out is removed; the head is written only when the order, the set of seqs or the counts changed. A put of the same list again writes nothing. Reading: the list in its order; the items after a position, which reads the head and only the items whose seq is past that position; the seq of the newest item; and whether any item has a value for a named field, read from the head alone when that field is indexed.

steps.title: Prove the objects on the example attempts
steps.do: In a throwaway place in the same store, with the same objects, keep these attempts in order, each through the store's own objects, each at the time given: [{"at": "2026-11-01T10:00:00Z", "list": "news", "indexed_fields": ["kind"], "items": [{"seq": 1, "kind": "a", "text": "x"}, {"seq": 2, "kind": "b", "text": "y"}]}, {"at": "2026-11-01T10:05:00Z", "list": "news", "indexed_fields": ["kind"], "items": [{"seq": 1, "kind": "a", "text": "x"}, {"seq": 2, "kind": "b", "text": "y"}]}, {"at": "2026-11-01T10:10:00Z", "list": "news", "indexed_fields": ["kind"], "items": [{"seq": 1, "kind": "a", "text": "x"}, {"seq": 2, "kind": "b", "text": "z"}, {"seq": 3, "kind": "a", "text": "w"}]}, {"at": "2026-11-01T10:15:00Z", "list": "news", "indexed_fields": ["kind"], "items": [{"seq": 1, "kind": "a", "text": "x"}, {"seq": 3, "kind": "a", "text": "w"}]}, {"at": "2026-11-01T10:20:00Z", "list": "news", "indexed_fields": ["kind"], "items": [{"seq": 1, "kind": "a", "text": "x"}, {"seq": 3, "kind": "a", "text": "w"}]}, {"at": "2026-11-01T10:25:00Z", "list": "news", "indexed_fields": ["kind"], "items": [{"kind": "a", "text": "no seq"}]}, {"at": "2026-11-01T10:30:00Z", "list": "news", "indexed_fields": ["kind"], "items": [{"seq": 3, "kind": "a", "text": "w"}, {"seq": 3, "kind": "a", "text": "again"}]}]. Each attempt must give the outcome the intent gives, and the store's own objects must give every expected answer below.

checks.says: Each put is kept, repeated or refused as the intent says
The store's own objects give every expected answer

steps.title: Keep this run's list
steps.do: Put the list items as given, through the store's own objects, and read the list back. Submit kept_ids (the list's name, when the put is kept or repeated), refused (the list's name and the store's own words for why) and found_ids (the list's name, when the list reads back). With no list given, submit three empty lists.

checks.says: Every list kept is read back
